item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Sat Oct 24, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Mercy Seminar, Term 3 — Thu Oct 29, 7:00 PM — Zoom Video Conferencing
item.description: With Father David Peck and Professor Randall Zachman Entirely on Zoom Now in its seventh year, the 2026 Mercy Seminar invites you to explore the profound insights that different faith traditions offer about embracing life and navigating death with grace. How can the certainty of death inspire us to cultivate a deeper focus and a heart full of gratitude, transforming potential feelings of anxiety into a courageous appreciation for the present moment? Is death merely “nothing at all,” or does it open the gateway to an eternal adventure beyond this life? Join us as we delve into selected sacred readings from Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish, Christian, and Muslim scriptures, along with enlightening contemporary secular spiritual writings. Together, we will uncover the wisdom that encourages us to live our best lives and face death not with fear, but with hope and understanding. item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Oct 29, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

item.title: White House Workers — Thu Oct 29, 5:30 PM — LancasterHistory
item.description:
Join White House Historical Association historian Sarah Fling as she highlights lesser-known stories of White House workers throughout history, including the men and women who worked for President James Buchanan.
Sarah Fling is a historian at the White House Historical Association. Her research focuses on free and enslaved workers, the first ladies, and the White House Collection. Fling is a contributor in The Cambridge Companion to US First Ladies (2025) and has published her research in White House History Quarterly and Teen Vogue. She serves on the Board of the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History, and previously served as a Community Lead in the Youth250 Bureau, a non-partisan initiative that highlighted the Gen Z perspective during America’s 250th. Sarah’s previous work experience includes internships at historic sites such as George Washington’s Mount Vernon and the Frick Pittsburgh. She received her bachelor’s degree in History from the University of Pittsburgh
